STRATEGY: Parent is a strategy in an iterated PD tournament; the trace simulates opponents (TFT, always C, always D, Pavlov, etc.) and designs an adaptive probe/exploit/TFT strategy, changing the parent by adding early probing, exploit mode, forgiveness, and last-round defection.

--- PART 2/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Use these general suggestions while pursuing the stated tournament objective."
STRATEGY: The parent is a Tit-for-Tat-like strategy with an early probe to detect unconditional cooperators, then exploit them. The trace simulates this probe-and-exploit design against Always C, TFT, Always D, and alternating defectors. The trace changes the probe timing, forgiveness rules, and state transitions to avoid DD spirals and recover cooperation after retaliation.

--- PART 3/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Use these general suggestions while pursuing the stated tournament objective."
STRATEGY: The parent is a Tit-for-Tat-like strategy with a one-time probe: cooperate initially, defect at round 5 if the opponent has never defected, then forgive retaliation or exploit continued cooperation, and defect on the final round. The trace simulated this strategy against TFT, Always C, Always D, and a defect-then-cooperate opponent. The trace revised the probe/forgiveness logic into a cleaner history-only implementation and kept the final-round defection.
